trust_decision.summary: Whether a `lng` or `ns` value may be interpolated into a loadPath/addPath template is decided by a per-key URL-segment denylist: `isSafeUrlSegmentBase` is shared, `isSafeLangUrlSegment` additionally rejects `/` and `@`, `isSafeNsUrlSegment` allows both, and `interpolateUrl` consults them via `SAFETY_CHECK_BY_KEY` (unknown keys fall back to strict) before `_readAny`/`create` hand the built URL to `options.request`. At the pinned commit the shared denylist omits `:` and the ns helper omits `//`, so a template that starts with the placeholder (e.g. `{{lng}}/{{ns}}.json`) becomes an absolute or protocol-relative URL.

landing_point.why: The summary says 'incomplete URL validation', and the repo has exactly one URL validator: the shared denylist in lib/utils.js. An engineer greps the validator, sees `/[?#%\s]/` with no `:` and an ns helper that is a bare pass-through, and starts there; nothing in the summary points at the checked-in browser bundles or at the addPath route.

fix_sites.entry_point: the same loadPath path, plus Backend.create -> interpolateUrl on addPath (lib/index.js:120,133)
window.i18nextHttpBackend (IIFE bundle loaded by <script>/CDN, README.md:71-73,103) -> read/readMulti -> _readAny (i18nextHttpBackend.js:260)

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: i18nextHttpBackend.js:17 and i18nextHttpBackend.js:26-28 (third copy at i18nextHttpBackend.min.js:1)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: i18nextHttpBackend.js/.min.js are tsdown output (tsdown.config.ts:31-53) that `npm run build` regenerates, and no test imports them (test/http.spec.js:2 loads ../index.js -> lib/index.js), so they read as generated artifacts not to be hand-edited; separately, loadUrl() receives a finished URL from its caller, so it looks like it has nothing to validate.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Nested-namespace and scoped-package namespace names must keep fetching: `a/b`, `foo/bar/baz` and `@organization/package-name` are documented-as-common shapes that earlier releases deliberately relaxed (3.0.6 allowed `/`, 4.0.1 allowed `@`), so the ns check must reject only `//`, not every `/`. Likewise arbitrary lng shapes (`pirate-speak`, `my-custom.ns`, `zh-Hant-HK`) and `+`-joined multi-values must keep working. An over-broad fix — blocking `/` in ns to kill `//`, or replacing the denylist with a BCP-47 allowlist — breaks them.

O6_input_shapes: plain lng string carrying a scheme delimiter: `http:127.0.0.1:8080` (rejected by the new `:` in the shared denylist)
plain ns string carrying a scheme delimiter: `http:127.0.0.1:8080/x`
protocol-relative ns: `//evil.example/x` and an embedded `a//b` (new ns-only `//` check; a single `/` stays allowed)
`+`-joined multi-value where only one segment carries the payload: `en+http:127.0.0.1:8080` — the check splits on `+` and validates each segment (lib/utils.js:155-161, fix.diff:141)
placeholder order: template starting with `{{lng}}` (`{{lng}}/{{ns}}.json`) and with `{{ns}}` (`{{ns}}/{{lng}}.json`) (fix.diff:135-140)
single string (read/create) vs array (readMulti) — both are flattened with join('+') at lib/index.js:64 and re-split inside interpolateUrl

O7_producer.where: lib/index.js:64 joins languages/namespaces with '+' into the single value handed to interpolateUrl (lib/index.js:133 passes the raw string for create), and lib/utils.js:155 re-splits on '+' — the producer and the checked item are the same handler, so the check does see what it validates

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Backend.loadUrl(url, callback, languages, namespaces) is a public, typed method (index.d.ts:126-131) that hands the caller-supplied URL straight to this.options.request without any interpolateUrl/segment check, so a URL built from lng/ns by the caller reaches the same request sink unvalidated
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: loadUrl is the low-level request primitive: it takes an already-built URL, there is no `{{lng}}`/`{{ns}}` template to interpolate, so validation looks like the caller's job — and the advisory is written about lng/ns values, which loadUrl never sees.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same file as the checked call sites (lib/index.js), one method below _readAny; the bundle copy is i18nextHttpBackend.js:272-277

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A second URL-building entry point on the class (e.g. a preload/readFromPath helper that interpolates a template and requests it)
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: loadUrl already shows the shape — a public method that talks to this.options.request directly and is documented in the typings; a maintainer adding preload or multi-load support would copy it rather than route through _readAny.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A lng/ns-aware query-string builder alongside queryStringParams (e.g. `?lng={{lng}}&ns={{ns}}`)
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: addQueryString already assembles URL fragments from option values, so letting queryStringParams accept per-request templates is a one-line feature that would bypass interpolateUrl entirely.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A third checked-in browser build (e.g. i18nextHttpBackend.esm.js) carrying its own copy of the denylist
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The config already emits two committed IIFE files whose copies of isSafeUrlSegmentBase had to be patched in the same commit; adding another output repeats that pattern.

O9_family: URL injection / SSRF — incomplete denylist on values interpolated into a request URL (CWE-918, CWE-74)

O10_build.toolchain: npm; tsdown (rolldown/oxc) builds esm/, cjs/ and the two root IIFE bundles; mocha 11 + expect.js for tests; eslint 9 / neostandard; tsc --noEmit + tsd for types
O10_build.project_tests: test/security.spec.js (denylist unit tests + interpolateUrl cases), test/http.spec.js:11 (read/readMulti/create against the localhost fixture, alternateFetch spy at test/http.spec.js:21), test/backendConnector.load.spec.js, test/request.spec.js, test/deno/*. No test imports the root IIFE bundles.

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Add `:` to the denylist in lib/utils.js and stop — leaving the ns `//` case, the addPath route and the checked-in bundles untouched — or over-correct by rejecting `/` (or `@`) in ns, which breaks nested namespaces and scoped-package names.

out_of_scope_notes: The denylist is re-exported as the backwards-compatible alias isSafeUrlSegment (lib/utils.js:68) for external callers; copies of it in other i18next backends are outside this repository.
README.md:219 documents the reloadInterval timer trap, which is a separate lifecycle issue and not part of this advisory.
unverified: repo_mb could not be measured (no shell in this session). tiny_repo is inferred from the tree: lib/ is three files, the largest committed artifact is the ~7 KB minified bundle, and the 138-file listing is dominated by small example JSON/JS; the MB value is left null.
present_in_latest for the O8 route: only the pinned tree and the fix diff were available ('latest release: none', no network), so it is unknown whether loadUrl is still unvalidated today.

The root IIFE bundles are regenerated by `npm run build`, which `npm test` runs (package.json:66,70); whether the benchmark's test command builds before testing was not checked, so whether a lib-only fix leaves the committed bundles stale depends on the harness.

`interpolate` (lib/utils.js:134) applies no segment check at all, but it is not reachable through the package `exports` map (package.json:11-31) and is not re-exported by index.js, so it was not counted as a public route.

O1 counted from the call sites of interpolateUrl (lib/index.js:64,133): read, readMulti, create. reload() reaches the same check indirectly through backendConnector.read and was not counted separately; the browser bundle exposes the same three methods rather than a fourth API.
